text: Baseline first: the box, board, ramp and empty scenes are recorded with RGB + amplitude after ground-detection-robustness run 4, without rclpy probes on the client, and their replay numbers (guidance off, gate off) are written down before anything is tuned; ground truth from the ChArUco board pose.

ToF amplitude guidance: per-pixel confidence from the pixel-aligned amplitude image; low-amplitude pixels dropped so the albedo bias on the printed board drops to p95 |h| <= 2 cm while >= 95 % of the floor 0.3-2.0 m is kept.

RGB-guided edges: boundaries of depth-detected lethal regions (obstacles, drops) snapped to RGB edges through the head_rgbd_cpp guided upsampling, so the box edge error drops from ~5 cm to <= 2 cm on replay.

No-return areas: where the RGB sees non-floor and the ToF has no returns (the black ramp) a no_return caution warning area is published, never free and never lethal, with null heights accepted by costmap_zones, mcp_server and web_ui.
RGB never creates a lethal obstacle by itself, heights only from depth; texture-only edges on flat floor (board, tile seams, shadows) do not add obstacles.
Replay recordings that include RGB + amplitude, replay tests against the measured ground truth, the Pi 5 CPU budget measured, and README/runbook/tests updated.
Graded traversability cost declined: the free / warning / lethal tiers and the rule (step > 0.04 m or slope > 15 deg) stay unchanged.

No new nodes; C++ for robot nodes except web_ui and mcp_server; live data via the web_ui websocket only, never rclpy probes on the client; recordings with the robot static and charging, head moves allowed.

User 2026-10-22, "Go for all 3 within one epic", item 1, ground detection on the live scene: record THIS scene (box, ramp, board; the new layout ahead/right of the robot) with a recorder that does not use ad-hoc rclpy on the client (the web-ui-ground-recorder-api and ground-record-script tasks), add it as replay fixtures with measured truth, fix the estimator until the live acceptance passes (box lethal >= 95 %, board never lethal, no lethal on empty floor at p95, churn < 10 %), then turn ground_voxel_layer back on and verify Nav2 reaches a goal across the scene. The unmet live acceptance of ground-detection-robustness moves into this epic; live steps need the user (scene in place, light on, robot static, head moves allowed, driving only short slow goals with the user present).

User 2026-10-22, "Go for all 3 within one epic", item 2, ToF flying-pixel filter retune: nodes/bridges/arducam_tof flying_pixel_filter (3x3 jump > max(30 mm, 5 % depth)) removed ~70 % of live pixels and is off in client.yml; retune it on real recorded depth frames (raw depth recordings, same recorder), keep >= 95 % of floor pixels, remove mixed pixels at the box edges, then turn it back on.

User 2026-10-22, "Go for all 3 within one epic", item 3: the approved head-and-arm calibration plan (head-and-arm-calibration-fro, 20 tasks, approvals H1-H9, gate answers HQ1-HQ4) and the approved RGB and amplitude plan (A1-A8, Q1-Q4) live in this one epic, with their tasks, requirement/AC text, approvals and decisions kept; the arm-joint-offsets follow-up epic stays separate.

User 2026-10-22: calibrate the head position/angles based on the arm position/angles (the arm is trusted as calibrated): the solve fits the head chain (mount x/y/z, yaw/pitch/roll, pan zero, tilt zero, tilt roll as observable) from the 6x5 ChArUco board clipped to the gripper, seen by the head camera over a scripted set of arm poses, with the floor-fit values as prior/cross-check.

Arm safety (project rules): least dramatic joints first; any pose moving shoulder_pan, shoulder_lift or elbow needs the user's explicit OK at run time (UI confirmation); every scripted pose FK-checked against self-collision with the robot body and head; wrist roll only half-open and lifted; negative elbow stretches; the existing 6x5 board is the gripper board; arm motion only through mcp_server's guarded tools; no driving (robot charging).
The result must pass held-out validation limits before Apply (like the floor fit); a result over any limit cannot be applied.

The applied result reaches every head-chain consumer through the existing head_chain.json override: head_state_publisher, mcp_server HeadKinematics and front camera (no mcp_server restart), and the web UI head URDF.
A guided step-by-step Head from arm section on the web UI Calibrate page (step cards for the physical steps, confirms, result, Apply).
Gate Q1 (kept): after the reprint the head tilt range is -30..+60 deg (+ is down) everywhere it is pinned, or the smaller tilt-down limit the user records.
Synthetic-scene tests for the fit and the pose check, READMEs and tests/README.md, and a runbook executed on the robot with real numbers.

User 2026-10-22: the arm joint offset solve (arm-offsets-plate-solver, arm-offsets-compute-apply, arm-calibrate-ui-section) moves to a separate follow-up epic via ticket.py (arm-joint-offsets-from-the-g, blocked by this one), not deleted, so nothing is lost.

User 2026-10-22 approved (yes): the Nav2 check drives two goals of at most 1.5 m (across the scene around the box, then back) through the mcp_server navigation tools at Nav2 0.25 m/s cap, with the user at the robot and the robot undocked by the user (D25)

User 2026-10-22 (answer C, "see retros from live robot - especially 2nd", item 1): collision_monitor raised collision_stop with polygon 'invalid source' during navigate_to_pose's final rotation (spurious; nearest lidar 0.7 m): a source (scan / tof_obstacles / tof_cliff, source_timeout 1.0 s) went stale; diagnose from Mimir/Loki and fix (source rates/QoS/timeout, or stale-source handling) so the final turn is not cut.

User 2026-10-22 (answer C, item 2): "Front camera has no intrinsics, so pixel_to_ground / mark_candidate_points can't use it" (mcp_server): find which camera mcp calls front and where intrinsics should come from (head_rgbd_calibration RGB intrinsics / camera_info), wire them; object positions must stop being 0.3-0.5 m guesses.

User 2026-10-22 (answer C, item 5): floor-level mirror wardrobe makes lidar ghost free space and ghost frontiers: a mirror mitigation (filter or person-drawn keep-out the agent honours) as a task.

User 2026-10-22 (answer C): agent behaviour items (arm parking, frontier choice, batching) are prompt/skill work: one task for the agent skills if they are not already covered.
